facts.raw_span: A 59-year-old man with a history of diabetes mellitus
one day of left-sided weakness, left facial paresis, difficulty speaking, and drowsiness
NIH Stroke Scale score on admission was 10
He denied recent head trauma or family history of stroke or thrombosis
He was a non-smoker but used opiates
Temperature was 37.4 °C
blood pressure 150/90 mm Hg
heart rate 73 bpm
An ECG showed normal sinus rhythm
a noncontrast head CT performed >24 h after symptom onset revealed an acute right MCA territory infarct in the right parietotemporal lobe
platelet count of 77 × 10^3/μL
Peripheral blood smear showed occasional schistocytes

contradict_spans: He denied recent head trauma or family history of stroke or thrombosis
support_spans: a noncontrast head CT performed >24 h after symptom onset revealed an acute right MCA territory infarct in the right parietotemporal lobe

concepts.why: Autoantibody-mediated hypercoagulability is the process that unifies the findings of recurrent thrombosis

finalists.label: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura
finalists.why: It has the strongest for evidence, including a low platelet count, schistocytes on the peripheral blood smear, and elevated LDH and bilirubin levels.

finalists.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
finalists.why: It has specific for evidence, including multiple infarcts in different territories, which suggests a prothrombotic state.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and renal dysfunction, as evidenced by the low platelet count, schistocytes, and elevated LDH and bilirubin levels, makes Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura the most likely diagnosis.
